content:
Hi! I'm working on first Mathlib contribution and I'd like to check naming / placement before opening a PR.

I want to add transport of a Finpartition along a type equivalence. Mathlib has Finpartition.map (transport along a lattice order-iso) and Finpartition.copy (re-casts a partition to an equal base), but nothing for relabelling the underlying elements of a set partition. The construction reuses Finpartition.map because a type equiv ι ≃ κ induces an order-iso on powersets.

Two new pieces:

namespace Equiv
/-- The order isomorphism `Finset α ≃o Finset β` induced by an equivalence `e : α ≃ β`,
the order-isomorphism refinement of `Equiv.finsetCongr`. -/
def finsetCongrOrderIso (e : α ≃ β) : Finset α ≃o Finset β
...

namespace Finpartition
/-- Transport a partition of `univ : Finset ι` along a type equivalence `e : ι ≃ κ`,
relabelling the underlying elements. -/
protected def congr (e : ι ≃ κ) (P : Finpartition (univ : Finset ι)) :
    Finpartition (univ : Finset κ)
...

plus the expected parts / refl / round-trip lemmas.

Q1) Naming
Is Finpartition.congr acceptable? I made it protected because of the congr tactic (and core congr_* lemmas). There's precedent for .congr as "transport along an equivalence": Set.congr/Quotient.congr return an Equiv, and Function.Embedding.congr transports a single value, like this does. My hesitation is that it also reads as congruence ("equal inputs ⇒ equal outputs").

Is congr fine here, or would you prefer mapEquiv (parallels map, already taken for the order-iso version) or relabel?

Q2) Placement of finsetCongrOrderIso
I put it in Data/Finset/Image.lean, right next to Equiv.finsetCongr and Finset.mapEmbedding which it mirrors. It has a lemma (e.finsetCongrOrderIso univ = univ) that needs Fintype, and the natural one-liner map_univ_equiv lives downstream in Data/Finset/BooleanAlgebra.lean, so I proved it inline in Image.lean rather than putting the def in BooleanAlgebra.lean (which is about the Boolean-algebra structure and seemed an unrelated home).

Is that the right call, or would you prefer finsetCongrOrderIso (or just its _univ lemma) to live in BooleanAlgebra.lean next to map_univ_equiv?

Context: this is the reusable (and hopefully useful) core for some set-partition ↔ Stirling/Bell Nat.card bridges I'm working toward. Thanks!
We already have docs#Equiv.finsetCongr, so I think we should name the Finset α ≃o Finset β orderiso something similar

I currently have Equiv.finsetCongrOrderIso (following finSuccAboveOrderIso/castOrderIso).

One thing I noticed though: the Set analogue already exists as Equiv.toOrderIsoSet : Set α ≃o Set β, which uses the toOrderIso_ naming rather than being derived from a congr. So there are two conventions.

Do you prefer finsetCongrOrderIso (parallels finsetCongr) or toOrderIsoFinset (parallels toOrderIsoSet)? Happy either way. Thanks!

You can try include a result as an docs#OrderType statement too maybe (for same universe , shameless plug really ) :see_no_evil: it would be equivalent to the conclusion , but may not really be worth it
